messages:
maria: Dropping a proposal for the limit-controller fallback ordering and telemetry. Short version: prefer a bounded soft-queue + polite client slowdown headers as the first line of backpressure, then a hard queue with fast eviction, then immediate 429s for abusive clients. Reserve 503 for infra-level failures only. Looking for: implementation pitfalls, header names, and what we should surface in the Console for rollouts/alerts.

sam: +1 to soft-queue first. key point: per-org burst credits need to be explicit so we don't let one org stall the entire pool. soft-queue should be time-limited (e.g. 250–500ms hold) and expose remaining queue position to clients so they can decide.

li: Curious about the client-visible UX here. Are we telling clients to poll while queued? I worry about thundering herd. Maybe return a small token and instruct exponential backoff with `Retry-After`.

maria: Good call. My thinking: soft-queue returns 202 with headers: `X-RI-Queue-Pos`, `X-RI-Queue-Est-ms`, `X-RI-Slowdown: <multiplier>` for polite clients. If client accepts, it can hold connection or re-POST the token. For short holds we can keep connection open and stream when ready (preferable).

jon: Streaming is great for first-party apps but third-party clients might not keep connections. Fallback: short-lived poll token (ttl 5s). But we must bound in-flight connections vs queued tokens to avoid memory blowup.

anya: About 429 vs 503: I'd rather 429 for client-caused rate limits and for soft rejections. 503 should be reserved for node oom/redis outage etc. We need a clear log field `limit.fallback.reason` that says `soft_queue|hard_queue|immediate_429|infra_503`.

sam: Agreed. Also add `X-RI-Backoff: rpc=100ms; jitter=0.2` style header to give clients guidance. People will ignore free-form text; a tiny structured header helps SDKs.

li: Telemetry suggestions: emit counters/histograms per org: `limit.queue.depth`, `limit.queue.wait_ms`, `limit.shed.429_count`, `limit.shed.503_count`, and a tag for `fallback_reason`. Also sample traces with `fallback.v=2` so we can compare rollout.

maria: Implementation sketch (router pseudocode):
```
if (org.has_burst_credits()) {
  accept_fast_path();
} else if (soft_queue_enabled && queue.depth(org) < soft_queue_limit) {
  enqueue_short_hold(); // keep connection open up to 500ms
  return 202 + X-RI-Queue-Pos + X-RI-Slowdown
} else if (hard_queue_enabled && global_hard_queue < hard_limit) {
  enqueue_hard(); // ttl token for client poll
  return 202 + X-RI-Queue-Token
} else {
  return 429 + Retry-After + X-RI-Shed-Reason=immediate_429
}
```

jon: Two implementation risks: 1) slow clients holding connections = file descriptor exhaustion; 2) inaccurate queue position when nodes fail over. Need eviction and conservative position estimates.

maria: Mitigations: enforce per-org connection cap, and always include `X-RI-Queue-Est-ms` as a range (e.g., "200-500ms"). For cross-node queue we can keep position as "<=N" rather than exact.

devops-bot: [alert] router-prod: soft-queue-depth at 82% of soft_limit in us-west-2 (since 03:22 UTC). Suggest throttling new rollouts for 10m.

sam: Good catch — we should have an autoscaling signal from queue depth to temporarily raise preemptible capacity or disable soft-queue to protect latency. Add an SLO: 95th tail for accept latency must not exceed 800ms even during soft-queue spikes.

anya: Console UX: add a "Backpressure" card per org that shows: current queue depth, recent soft-queue rate, average wait_ms, and a graph of `limit.fallback.reason` split. Also expose a toggle in org settings: `prefer_soft_queue` and a rollout flag so SEs can flip for specific customers.

li: Rollout plan: feature-flag `limit_fallback_v2` -> 1% orgs (no burst credits for test orgs) -> 10% (monitor) -> 50% -> 100%. Measure: change in token_cost, 95th latency, and `limit.shed.429_count`.

maria: Questions for final decision: a) header names (we proposed X-RI-Queue-Pos, X-RI-Queue-Est-ms, X-RI-Slowdown, X-RI-Queue-Token, X-RI-Shed-Reason), b) whether 202 is an OK interim status for queued requests, c) maximum soft-hold ms (propose 500ms), d) telemetry chart set.

jon: My votes: a) header names fine, b) 202 OK if we keep a streaming path for prefer-connected clients, c) 500ms is upper bound — prefer 250ms to reduce fd pressure, d) include `limit.queue.latency_p50/p95/p99` in dashboards.

sam: vote: same as jon but OK with 500ms for first rollout; circuit-break to 250ms if queue depth > 75%.

anya: I'll draft the Console card mock and the telemetry dashboard. Also will add a runbook mapping `Shed-Reason` to alerts (e.g., `immediate_429` -> customer contact, `infra_503` -> pager).

maria: Thanks all. I'll update the design doc with these decisions and a short experiment checklist: feature flag, telemetry, dashboard, rollout cadence, and the autoscale/disable-soft-queue circuit. Planning to land a small prototype PR for the router this sprint.

li: one last nit — ensure SDKs can interpret `X-RI-Slowdown` multiplier; open PR for node/python SDKs to map to backoff logic.

maria: noted. thanks! :thumbsup:
